---
title: "Measured performance (on your machine)"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Measured performance (on your machine)}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 110)
library(simdfuse)

# Everything on this page is measured when the vignette is built. Nothing is
# read from a stored results file, so the numbers below describe the machine
# that built this document rather than the author's.
bench_file <- system.file("benchmarks", "benchmarks.R", package = "simdfuse")
if (!nzchar(bench_file)) bench_file <- "../inst/benchmarks/benchmarks.R"
source(bench_file)

# Size profile. "tiny" on CRAN, where a long-running vignette is unwelcome;
# "quick" for an ordinary local build; override with
#   SIMDFUSE_BENCH_SCALE=full R CMD build .
on_cran <- !identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true")
scale <- Sys.getenv("SIMDFUSE_BENCH_SCALE", if (on_cran) "tiny" else "quick")
prof <- sf_bench_profile(scale)

set.seed(20260114)
elapsed <- system.time(res <- sf_bench_all(prof))[["elapsed"]]
si <- sf_bench_sysinfo()

# Measurement spread, used to say when a comparison is inside the noise.
spr <- function(bench, case, engine) {
  s <- res[res$bench == bench & res$case == case & res$engine == engine, ]
  if (nrow(s)) s$spread[1] else NA_real_
}
noisy <- function(...) isTRUE(spr(...) > 0.15)

sec <- function(bench, case, engine) {
  s <- res[res$bench == bench & res$case == case & res$engine == engine, ]
  if (nrow(s)) s$seconds[1] else NA_real_
}
ms  <- function(...) { v <- sec(...); if (is.na(v)) "--" else sprintf("%.1f", v * 1e3) }
sp  <- function(bench, case, num, den) {
  v <- sec(bench, case, num) / sec(bench, case, den)
  if (is.na(v)) NA_real_ else round(v, 2)
}
spx <- function(...) { v <- sp(...); if (is.na(v)) "--" else sprintf("%.2fx", v) }
fmt_n <- function(n) format(n, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
pal <- c("#1b6ca8", "#d1495b", "#66a182", "#edae49", "#2e4057")
mar <- function() par(mar = c(4.2, 4.4, 1.2, 1), las = 1, bty = "l",
                      mgp = c(2.6, 0.6, 0))

fus <- subset(res, bench == "fusion")
ops <- c("1 op", "2 ops", "4 ops", "8 ops", "16 ops"); opn <- c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
ns <- sort(unique(fus$n)); nmax <- max(ns)
sp_at <- function(nn, o) {
  s <- fus[fus$n == nn, ]
  s$seconds[s$case == o & s$engine == "base R"] /
    s$seconds[s$case == o & s$engine == "simdfuse"]
}
sp_big <- vapply(ops, function(o) sp_at(nmax, o), 0)
cross <- opn[which(sp_big >= 1)]
cross <- if (length(cross)) min(cross) else NA
```

A word on reading the numbers. Each measurement is the fastest of several
timed batches, and the spread across those batches is recorded alongside it.
On a shared or thermally throttled machine -- any laptop, and anything with
asymmetric cores -- repeated threaded measurements of the same expression can
differ by a quarter, which is larger than several of the effects compared here.
Where that happens the table below says so; treat those rows as indicative and
re-run before drawing a conclusion from them.

Every figure and number on this page was measured while this vignette was
being built, by the functions in `inst/benchmarks/benchmarks.R`. Nothing is
read from a stored results file. What follows therefore describes **your**
machine, and the same document built elsewhere will say something different.

```{r sysinfo, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf(
"| | |\n|---|---|\n| platform | %s |\n| R | %s |\n| instruction set in use | %s (%d lanes per register) |\n| backends available | %s |\n| cores | %s physical, %s logical |\n| OpenMP | %s, %d threads offered |\n%s%s| size profile | `%s` (n up to %s), %.0f s to measure |\n",
  si$platform, si$r_version, si$isa, si$lanes, si$available,
  ifelse(is.na(si$cores), "?", si$cores), ifelse(is.na(si$logical), "?", si$logical),
  if (isTRUE(si$openmp)) "yes" else "no", si$max_threads,
  if (!is.na(si$cache)) sprintf("| cache | %s |\n", si$cache) else "",
  if (!is.na(si$omp_env)) sprintf("| thread limits in the environment | `%s` |\n", si$omp_env) else "",
  prof$scale, fmt_n(max(prof$n_thread, nmax)), elapsed))
```

`r if (scale != "full") sprintf("The timings here use the **%s** profile, which keeps vector lengths modest so that building this vignette stays quick. The full profile uses vectors of %s elements, where the effects below are larger because the data no longer fits in any cache. To reproduce the author's numbers, run <code>Rscript inst/benchmarks/bench-run.R</code>.", scale, fmt_n(1e7)) else "This is the full profile."`

## Fusion

Base R evaluates an array expression one operator at a time, allocating and
traversing a vector per operator. simdfuse compiles the expression and makes a
single pass, keeping intermediates in cache. What is being removed is therefore
*traversals of memory*, and the benefit should grow both with the number of
operators and with `n`.

```{r fig-fusion, fig.height = 4.2}
mar()
plot(NA, xlim = c(1, 16), ylim = range(0.5, unlist(lapply(ns, function(nn)
       vapply(ops, function(o) sp_at(nn, o), 0))) * 1.12),
     log = "x", xaxt = "n", xlab = "arithmetic operations in the expression",
     ylab = "speedup over base R (x)")
axis(1, at = opn, labels = opn)
abline(h = 1, col = "grey60", lty = 2)
for (i in seq_along(ns))
  lines(opn, vapply(ops, function(o) sp_at(ns[i], o), 0), col = pal[i],
        lwd = 2.4, type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.9)
legend("topleft", sprintf("n = %s", fmt_n(ns)), col = pal[seq_along(ns)],
       lwd = 2.4, pch = 19, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
```

At the largest length measured here, n = `r fmt_n(nmax)`, the sixteen-operator
expression ran **`r sprintf("%.2fx", sp_big[["16 ops"]])`** and the
eight-operator one **`r sprintf("%.2fx", sp_big[["8 ops"]])`**. The single
operator case ran `r sprintf("%.2fx", sp_big[["1 op"]])`, that is
`r if (sp_big[["1 op"]] >= 1) "still faster" else "**slower** than base R"`.

`r if (is.na(cross)) "On this machine no expression depth measured here came out ahead, which is worth knowing before you adopt the package." else if (cross == 1) "Every depth measured came out ahead on this machine." else sprintf("The crossover is at **%d operators**: below that there is no temporary worth eliminating and only the interpreter's own overhead remains. If your expressions are single operations, this package has nothing to offer you.", cross)`

## Elementary functions

Base R calls the platform `libm` once per element for `exp()` and `log()`, and
no auto-vectoriser can change that because it cannot see inside the library
call. The default `math = "accurate"` mode makes the same calls, so it is
expected to sit near parity; `math = "fast"` substitutes SIMD polynomials.

```{r tab-mathfun, results = "asis"}
cat("| expression | base R | accurate | fast | fast speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
for (l in c("exp(x)", "log(x)", "sqrt(x)", "gaussian loglik"))
  cat(sprintf("| `%s` | %s ms | %s ms | %s ms | %s |\n", l,
      ms("mathfun", l, "base R"), ms("mathfun", l, "simdfuse accurate"),
      ms("mathfun", l, "simdfuse fast"),
      spx("mathfun", l, "base R", "simdfuse fast")))
```

```{r mathfun-prose, results = "asis"}
labs <- c("exp(x)", "log(x)", "sqrt(x)", "gaussian loglik")
slow <- labs[vapply(labs, function(l)
  isTRUE(sec("mathfun", l, "simdfuse accurate") > sec("mathfun", l, "base R") * 1.05), TRUE)]
if (length(slow))
  cat(sprintf("At this scale the accurate mode came out *slower* than base R on %s. The block interpreter has a fixed per-call and per-block cost, and it only pays for itself once an expression has several operators or the data stops fitting in cache -- see the crossover above. The fast column is a different trade: it buys speed with a documented 1-4 ulp error, which `vignette(\"accuracy\")` quantifies.\n",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", slow), collapse = ", ")))
```

The sweep below is the measurement that separates the SIMD contribution from
the fusion contribution: identical work, identical data, one backend per bar.

```{r fig-isa, fig.height = 3.6}
ord <- c("scalar", "sse2", "avx2", "avx512", "neon")
e <- subset(res, bench == "isa_exp")
e <- e[order(match(e$case, ord)), ]
mar()
bp <- barplot(e$seconds * 1e3, names.arg = e$case, col = pal[1], border = NA,
              ylab = sprintf("ms for exp(), n = %s", fmt_n(e$n[1])),
              ylim = c(0, max(e$seconds * 1e3) * 1.22))
text(bp, e$seconds * 1e3, sprintf("%.1f", e$seconds * 1e3), pos = 3, cex = 0.8)
if (nrow(e) > 1)
  text(bp, e$seconds * 1e3 / 2, sprintf("%.2fx", e$seconds[1] / e$seconds),
       col = "white", font = 2, cex = 0.9)
```

```{r isa-prose, results = "asis"}
if (nrow(e) > 1) {
  r <- e$seconds[1] / e$seconds[nrow(e)]
  verdict <- if (r < si$lanes * 0.9)
    "The shortfall against that ideal is memory traffic, which no amount of arithmetic width removes."
  else if (r > si$lanes * 1.1)
    "It exceeds the lane ratio, which happens because the narrow backends pay more per-element loop overhead as well as doing narrower arithmetic."
  else "That is close to the ideal."
  cat(sprintf("Scalar to %s is a factor of **%.2f** on this CPU, against a lane ratio of %d. %s For plain `+` and `*` the same sweep is far flatter, because R's own loops already auto-vectorise and the expression is bandwidth-bound: the SIMD layer earns its keep on the transcendentals.\n",
      e$case[nrow(e)], r, si$lanes, verdict))
} else {
  cat("Only one backend is available on this CPU, so there is nothing to compare.\n")
}
```

## Reductions

A reduction is fused into the expression and never allocates a result vector,
so `sum((x - mu)^2)` runs in constant auxiliary memory whatever the length of
`x`.

```{r fig-reduce, fig.height = 4.2}
rr <- subset(res, bench == "reduce"); cs <- unique(rr$case)
eng <- c("base R", "simdfuse 1 thread", "simdfuse all threads")
m <- sapply(cs, function(c0) vapply(eng, function(en) sec("reduce", c0, en), 0)) * 1e3
mar(); par(mar = c(5.4, 4.4, 1.2, 1))
bp <- barplot(m, beside = TRUE, col = pal[1:3], border = NA, names.arg = cs,
              ylab = sprintf("ms, n = %s", fmt_n(rr$n[1])), las = 2,
              ylim = c(0, max(m, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.24), cex.names = 0.72)
legend("topright", eng, fill = pal[1:3], border = NA, bty = "n", cex = 0.78)
for (j in seq_len(ncol(m)))
  text(bp[2:3, j], m[2:3, j], sprintf("%.1fx", m[1, j] / m[2:3, j]), pos = 3, cex = 0.66)
```

```{r reduce-prose, results = "asis"}
best <- cs[which.max(vapply(cs, function(c0)
  sec("reduce", c0, "base R") / sec("reduce", c0, "simdfuse 1 thread"), 0))]
cat(sprintf("`%s` gained most (%s on one thread): base R builds and discards a full vector to produce one number. `sum(x)` gains least (%s), because there is no temporary to remove, only the summation itself",
    best, spx("reduce", best, "base R", "simdfuse 1 thread"),
    spx("reduce", "sum(x)", "base R", "simdfuse 1 thread")))
if (!is.na(sec("reduce", "sum(x)", "collapse::fsum")))
  cat(sprintf(" -- and `collapse::fsum` takes %s ms against our %s ms",
      ms("reduce", "sum(x)", "collapse::fsum"),
      ms("reduce", "sum(x)", "simdfuse all threads")))
cat(".\n\n")
mb <- sec("memory", "sum((x-mu)^2+sqrt(x))", "base R")
msf <- sec("memory", "sum((x-mu)^2+sqrt(x))", "simdfuse")
cat(sprintf("Peak memory for `sum((x - mu)^2 + sqrt(x))` at n = %s: **%.0f MiB** for base R against **%.0f MiB** fused. Both include the %.0f MiB input itself, which neither approach avoids; the difference is the temporaries.\n",
    fmt_n(prof$n), mb, msf, prof$n * 8 / 2^20))
```

## Skeletons

```{r tab-skel, results = "asis"}
cat("| operation | alternative | simdfuse | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n")
rows <- list(
  list("5-point stencil", "stencil", "5-point mean", "stats::filter"),
  list("5-point stencil", "stencil", "5-point mean", "data.table::frollmean"),
  list("sum by group",    "segreduce", "sum by group", "base rowsum"),
  list("sum by group",    "segreduce", "sum by group", "collapse::fsum"),
  list("cumsum(log(x))",  "scan", "cumsum(log(x))", "base R"),
  list("cumsum(x)",       "scan", "cumsum", "base R"))
for (w in rows) {
  alt <- sec(w[[2]], w[[3]], w[[4]])
  if (is.na(alt)) next
  mine <- if (w[[3]] == "cumsum") sec("scan", "cumsum", "simdfuse parallel")
          else sec(w[[2]], w[[3]], "simdfuse")
  flag <- if (noisy(w[[2]], w[[3]], "simdfuse") ||
              noisy(w[[2]], w[[3]], w[[4]])) " (noisy)" else ""
  cat(sprintf("| %s | `%s` %.1f ms | %.1f ms | %.2fx%s |\n", w[[1]], w[[4]],
              alt * 1e3, mine * 1e3, alt / mine, flag))
}
```

The grouped sum is not quite like for like: `rowsum` and `collapse::fsum`
accept groups in any order, while `sf_segreduce()` needs contiguous runs. On an
already-sorted panel that restriction is free; otherwise the sort dominates and
`collapse` is the better tool.

```{r scan-prose, results = "asis"}
s_par <- sp("scan", "cumsum", "base R", "simdfuse parallel")
s_log <- sp("scan", "cumsum(log(x))", "base R", "simdfuse")
cat(sprintf("The plain scan is the honest weak spot: `cumsum(x)` came out at %.2fx%s. A scan is memory-bound and the parallel form reads the data twice. Fusing a transformation into it recovers %.1f times that, with `cumsum(log(x))` at %.2fx, %s\n",
    s_par, if (s_par < 1) ", slower than base R" else "",
    s_log / s_par, s_log,
    if (s_log >= 1)
      "so the scan is worth using when there is an expression to fuse into it, and not otherwise."
    else
      "which on this machine is still short of base R: at this scale neither form of the scan is a reason to use the package. On the author's full-profile run the fused form did come out ahead."))
```

## Thread scaling

```{r fig-threads, fig.height = 3.6}
th <- subset(res, bench == "threads" & engine == "simdfuse")
th$k <- as.integer(th$case); th <- th[order(th$k), ]
base_t <- sec("threads", "base R", "base R")
mar()
if (nrow(th) > 1) {
  plot(th$k, th$seconds[1] / th$seconds, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2.4,
       col = pal[1], xlab = "threads", ylab = "speedup over 1 thread (x)",
       xaxt = "n", ylim = c(0.9, max(2, th$seconds[1] / min(th$seconds)) * 1.1))
  axis(1, at = th$k)
  abline(0, 1, col = "grey70", lty = 3)
  legend("topleft", c("measured", "perfect scaling"), col = c(pal[1], "grey70"),
         lwd = c(2.4, 1), lty = c(1, 3), pch = c(19, NA), bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
} else {
  plot.new(); text(0.5, 0.5, "only one thread available", cex = 1.1)
}
```

```{r thread-prose, results = "asis"}
if (nrow(th) > 1) {
  cat(sprintf("%.1f ms on one thread against %.1f ms on %d, a speedup of **%.2fx**; base R takes %.1f ms. This expression is bandwidth-bound, so it stops scaling well before the core count runs out -- do not read these numbers as a core-count law. Two further caveats: on a machine with asymmetric cores (Apple Silicon, Intel hybrid) OpenMP counts the efficiency cores too, and threads landing on them flatten the curve; and the sweep is capped at %d here%s.\n",
      th$seconds[1] * 1e3, min(th$seconds) * 1e3, th$k[which.min(th$seconds)],
      th$seconds[1] / min(th$seconds), base_t * 1e3, max(th$k),
      if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_")))
        ", which is R CMD check restricting cores rather than your hardware -- build the vignette outside check to see the whole curve"
      else if (!is.na(prof$thread_cap) && max(th$k) >= prof$thread_cap)
        sprintf(" by the `%s` size profile, not by your hardware", prof$scale)
      else " by what OpenMP reports"))
  if (!is.na(si$cores) && si$max_threads < si$cores) {
    cat(sprintf("\n**OpenMP is offering %d thread%s on a machine with %d physical cores**, so the sweep above is not measuring this hardware. %sBuild the vignette outside `R CMD check` -- `devtools::build_vignettes()`, or knit `vignettes/performance.Rmd` directly -- to see the real curve.\n",
        si$max_threads, if (si$max_threads == 1) "" else "s", si$cores,
        if (!is.na(si$omp_env))
          sprintf("The environment holds `%s`, which is where the limit comes from. ", si$omp_env)
        else if (isTRUE(si$under_check))
          "This looks like an `R CMD check` run, which restricts cores. "
        else ""))
  }
} else {
  cat("Threading could not be measured here.\n")
}
```

## Choosing the block size

The block is how many elements are processed per pass, and so how much of the
working set stays in L1. The package default is 128 doubles, one kibibyte per
register.

```{r fig-block, fig.height = 4}
b <- subset(res, bench == "block")
b$block <- as.integer(b$engine); cs <- unique(b$case)
rel <- lapply(cs, function(c0) { s <- b[b$case == c0, ]; s$seconds / min(s$seconds) })
mar()
plot(NA, xlim = range(b$block), ylim = c(0.95, max(unlist(rel)) * 1.05), log = "x",
     xlab = "block size (doubles per register)",
     ylab = "time relative to the best for that expression")
for (i in seq_along(cs)) {
  s <- b[b$case == cs[i], ]
  lines(s$block, s$seconds / min(s$seconds), col = pal[i], lwd = 2.2,
        type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.8)
}
abline(v = 128, col = "grey45", lty = 3)
legend("topleft", cs, col = pal[seq_along(cs)], lwd = 2.2, pch = 19, bty = "n",
       cex = 0.82)
```

```{r block-prose, results = "asis"}
bestb <- vapply(cs, function(c0) { s <- b[b$case == c0, ]; s$block[which.min(s$seconds)] }, 0)
cost128 <- vapply(cs, function(c0) {
  s <- b[b$case == c0, ]
  if (any(s$block == 128L)) 100 * (s$seconds[s$block == 128L] / min(s$seconds) - 1) else NA
}, 0)
cat(sprintf("On this machine the best block was %s, and the default of 128 cost %s relative to the best for each expression.\n\n",
    paste(sprintf("%d (%s)", bestb, cs), collapse = ", "),
    paste(sprintf("%+.0f%%", cost128), collapse = ", ")))
cat("The curve is usually not monotone, which is worth noticing: particular block sizes place the registers at strides that collide in a set-associative L1, and the penalty appears and disappears again as the size grows. The optimum is also strongly machine-specific -- measured best values have ranged from 64 doubles on an Intel Xeon to 2048 on an Apple M-series -- so rather than reasoning about it, run `sf_tune()` once on this machine and put the answer in your `.Rprofile`.\n")
```

## Reproducing and extending this

```{r repro, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
# the same functions this vignette just ran
source(system.file("benchmarks", "benchmarks.R", package = "simdfuse"))
res <- sf_bench_all(sf_bench_profile("quick"), verbose = TRUE)

# the author's full-scale run, several minutes and a few GB of memory
# Rscript inst/benchmarks/bench-run.R
```

Build this vignette at a different scale with the `SIMDFUSE_BENCH_SCALE`
environment variable, set to `tiny`, `quick` or `full`.
